question: Louis-Camille Maillard described sugars browning with amino acids in 1912. Who drew the map of it chemists still use?
answer: John Hodge, a chemist at the US Department of Agriculture, in 1953. For forty years the reaction had a name and only pieces of a mechanism. Hodge, studying browning in dried foods, laid out its stages in one diagram: early bonding, a middle of fragments, late brown polymers. Chemists still teach from it.
move: A name on a discovery says who noticed it, not who explained it.
reference: Hodge, Dehydrated foods: chemistry of browning reactions in model systems, Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry, 1953
